messages:
lena: Hey, hitting intermittent 504 / stalled streaming when using the Node TS SDK from an Edge function (Vercel). Starts fine then stops emitting chunks after ~1-2s. Repro and logs below.

sam: thanks for flagging — can you paste the SDK version + small repro?

lena: sdk@0.4.2, node 18 on Vercel edge. Minimal handler:```ts
export default async (req) => {
  const res = await Redwood.client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood/gpt-small', messages: [{role:'user', content:'hi'}] })
  for await (const chunk of res) {
    // forward chunk to client SSE
  }
  return new Response('ok')
} ```

lena: console shows initial chunks then: `TypeError: Response body is null` and client sees connection hang.

maya: does the edge runtime have the secret exposed? if token missing we sometimes see immediate 401 then retries. but you said initial chunks arrive so auth probably fine.

kevin: two likely suspects: 1) SDK streaming uses a Node ReadableStream API that isn't identical to Web Streams in edge. 2) Automatic retry logic in our client replays requests and causes stream body to be unavailable for subsequent attempts.

sam: can you confirm if you're using fetch-based streaming or Node stream helpers? Edge requires web ReadableStream usage.

lena: I'm using the SDK helper (res is an async iterator). I assumed SDK handles edge detection.

kevin: sdk@0.4.x had partial edge support; full edge-compatible streaming landed in 0.5. The retry path also used undrainable body handling before 0.5.

lena: aha. Is upgrading safe? any breaking changes?

kevin: minor API shape unchanged for chat.stream, but the internal transport changed. Recommend testing against 0.5.1-canary or stable 0.5.0. Also set explicit retry: 0 for streaming routes as a quick mitigation.

maya: quick repro tweak to validate it's an edge vs node issue: run the exact same handler in a Node Serverless function (not edge) — if it streams fine there, it's edge compatibility.

lena: tried serverless (node serverless) — streaming works reliably. Same code, same env. So it's edge-specific.

sam: good repro. Two short-term options: 1) upgrade SDK to >=0.5.0 which ships web-stream-friendly implementation, 2) move streaming endpoint to serverless (non-edge) until you upgrade.

lena: i also saw a billing spike for some of these failed/retried requests. any insight?

billing-bot: note: when automatic retries replay a streaming request we may charge for the initial token consumption if the upstream registers token usage before the retry triggers.

kevin: yes — the retry logic can accidentally double-send for streaming if the body is non-idempotent. Disable automatic retries for streaming routes:```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, retry: { maxRetries: 0 } })
```

lena: did that locally — stopped double charges but still saw hang on edge until upgrading.

sam: one more gotcha — Vercel Edge strips certain response streaming internals when you try to pipe Node stream methods. Make sure you rely on web ReadableStream methods (`response.body.getReader()` or async iterator on web stream) not Node's `stream.Readable` methods.

lena: what's the recommended SDK config to force web-stream mode?

kevin: in 0.5 the SDK auto-detects edge and uses web streams. For 0.4 you can monkeypatch globalThis.ReadableStream polyfill but it's hacky. Upgrade recommended.

maya: repro steps we've used to validate in support:
1) Deploy minimal edge function with sdk@0.4.2.
2) Hit endpoint and observe initial chunk then `Response body is null` in logs.
3) Change to serverless (node) — streaming OK.
4) Upgrade to sdk@0.5.1-canary — edge streaming stable.

lena: thanks. I'll try upgrading to 0.5.1-canary and redeploy. Any config to prevent auth issues?

sam: ensure token is available to edge functions — on Vercel tokens must be set as Edge Runtime compatible environment variable (not Dashboard Server-only secret). If token missing you'll get 401s and sometimes confusing retry behavior.

lena: token is set as a regular env var (VERCEL_ENV). I'll double-check the secret scope.

kevin: finally, if you need immediate mitigation and can't upgrade: implement a small proxy serverless function (node) that talks to Redwood streaming and re-exposes SSE to clients. It's slightly higher latency but stable.

lena: upgrading now. i'll report back. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started for support/lena/edge-test @ 2026-03-16T15:40:12Z

lena: upgrade to sdk@0.5.1-canary deployed — streaming looked good in canary tests, no stalls. will monitor production.

billing-bot: FYI we flagged a couple of double-billing events tied to retry on streaming routes; refunds queued for affected accounts.

sam: great — closing loop. If you still see any 504s after 0.5, ping with request IDs and a HAR or the function logs and we'll escalate to runtime team.

lena: will do. thanks team!
